previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, colorectal cancer, and prolonged QT syndrome, was admitted from rehab for failure to thrive and significant weight loss. He was cachectic and weak, with chronic diarrhea and poor oral intake. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with Klebsiella pneumoniae and new-onset right hydronephrosis due to urinary retention, likely from a bladder diverticulum. A Foley catheter was placed, leading to improvement in renal function. A Dobhoff feeding tube was inserted to address malnutrition, and tube feeds were initiated. The patient was started on IV ceftriaxone for the UTI, mirtazapine for appetite and mood, and levothyroxine for newly diagnosed hypothyroidism. His condition stabilized, with improved strength and tolerance of enteral nutrition. He was discharged to extended care with plans for urology follow-up for cystoscopy, continuation of antibiotics, and monitoring of fecal fat and CMV studies.

vascularity is normal.  There is no pneumothorax.  Osseous structures are
unchanged.  Cervical spinous fusion hardware is again noted.

IMPRESSION:  Chronic small right pleural effusion with right basilar
atelectasis.  Probable new trace left pleural effusion.
